pageSize stays in the 20-24 range (spec §2), never 1000 (spec §10).

openDecisions.question: How deep must the infinite scroll actually reach, given useLibraryBooks caps the page window?
openDecisions.context: apps/web/src/features/books/api/use-books.ts:13,23 sets `maxPages: 10`. With pageSize 20-24 that retains 200-240 rows; fetching page 11 evicts page 1, so the rendered list shifts instead of growing. The spec's acceptance line says 'вся library доступна через infinite scroll'.
options: (a) Accept the 10-page window: the backend search reaches anything deeper (q matches title, original title, authors, series, publisher, tags, translator, illustrator, isbn - apps/api/src/modules/books/infrastructure/book-search.ts:26-48).
(b) Give the picker its own infinite query in books/api without maxPages (~25 lines, zero blast radius on the 11 existing useLibraryBooks consumers).
(c) Remove or raise maxPages inside useLibraryBooks (touches the main library grid and 10 other consumers; memory risk).
openDecisions.recommendation: (a). A dialog picker with debounced backend search does not need unbounded depth, and (c) is a behaviour change to the library grid that no task asked for. Escalate to (b) only if the acceptance line is read literally.
openDecisions.answer: (d) NEW OPTION chosen by the user: make maxPages a configurable option on useLibraryBooks, keeping the existing default of 10 for all current consumers, and pass maxPages: 0 (TanStack Query = unlimited, verified in query-core utils.js addToEnd(items,item,max=0)) from BookSingleSelectPicker so every fetched page stays in data.pages and infinite scroll can walk the whole library. No separate picker-local infinite query. No global behaviour change. No hard 200-book limit. Search stays backend-driven through the same useLibraryBooks.

openDecisions.question: pageSize 20 or 24?
openDecisions.context: Spec §2 says 'приблизно 20-24'. Codebase: LIBRARY_PAGE_SIZE = 24 (apps/web/src/features/books/model/library-query.ts:25) is the library grid size; every dialog picker uses 20 (dedication-book-picker-dialog.tsx:29, add-book-to-queue-dialog.tsx:36, use-solo-books.ts:12, quotes/components/book-picker.tsx:23); BookMultiSelectPicker uses 24 (book-multi-select-picker.tsx:22).
openDecisions.recommendation: 20 - it matches every other single-select dialog picker and shortens the first paint inside a modal. Interacts with D1: 20 x 10 pages = 200 rows.
openDecisions.answer: (a) pageSize 20 - dialog-picker precedent (dedication-book-picker-dialog.tsx:29, add-book-to-queue-dialog.tsx:36). Decided by the orchestrator, not escalated.

openDecisions.question: Does edit mode get a working 'Змінити' that can move the quote to another book?
openDecisions.context: Spec §8 asks for it. The backend cannot do it and §2/§10 forbid a new endpoint: `UpdateQuoteInputSchema` has no bookId (packages/shared/src/quotes.ts:50-57) and the update call is scoped by the owning book id in the path (apps/web/src/features/quotes/api/use-quote-mutations.ts:55, controller route /api/books/:bookId/quotes/:quoteId). This is the one spec requirement the code cannot satisfy as written.
options: (a) Edit mode shows only the compact selected book, with no Змінити affordance; the picker's change mode is a create-mode capability.
(b) Edit mode renders the picker in a read-only/disabled state so the user sees why the book is fixed.
(c) Add a move-quote capability to the Quotes API (BE work, contradicts the no-new-endpoint constraint).
(d) FE-only 'move' by delete + recreate (non-atomic, loses the quote id and createdAt).
openDecisions.recommendation: (a), and record the deviation from §8 in the PR body. (d) is a data-loss pattern and (c) is out of the stated scope.
openDecisions.answer: (a) No backend work in this refactor. UpdateQuoteInputSchema keeps no bookId. create mode: full picker, then compact selected state with a Змінити button. edit mode: compact selected state of the current book immediately, NO Змінити button, picker never opens, submit sends no bookId, and no disabled/read-only book list is rendered. The §8 requirement for Змінити in edit mode is deliberately amended to match the current backend contract; record the deviation in the PR body.

openDecisions.question: Who owns the compact selected state - the new picker or the existing QuoteBookPreview?
openDecisions.context: The spec itself forks here (§8: 'прибрати дубль; або reuse QuoteBookPreview як selected state'). `QuoteBookPreview` is a private, unexported function inside apps/web/src/features/quotes/components/quote-dialog.tsx:235-269, rendered for every mode at quote-dialog.tsx:386, and its name collides with the exported shared type `QuoteBookPreview` (packages/shared/src/quotes.ts:143).
options: (a) The picker owns a generic compact selected row and the local QuoteBookPreview is deleted - one component, reusable by the next caller, but the Quotes-specific look (w-16 cover, font-heading title, user icon) is replaced by the books-feature row look.
(b) The picker takes a `renderSelected`/children slot and Quotes passes QuoteBookPreview - keeps the Quotes visual, costs one more prop (composition over props, docs/code-principles.md §4.7).
openDecisions.recommendation: (a). The compact card is a picker concern, not a quotes concern, and it is what makes the component reusable. Pick (b) only if the current Quotes visual is deliberate design; if so, rename the local component to avoid the shared-type collision.
openDecisions.answer: (a) with an explicit split: the compact selected UI is its own reusable presentation primitive at the Books feature level, NOT hidden privately inside the picker. BookSingleSelectPicker owns search/list plus the transition into the compact state; BookSingleSelectValue is the single representation of an already-selected book (cover + title + author + optional action). Quotes create mode renders the picker, which shows BookSingleSelectValue with a Змінити action; Quotes edit mode renders BookSingleSelectValue directly with no action. Delete the private QuoteBookPreview at quote-dialog.tsx:235-269. Do NOT add a renderSelected slot. Do NOT keep a Quotes-specific selected-book visual.

openDecisions.question: Where do the picker's strings live: a `labels` prop owned by each caller, or the picker's own i18n namespace?
openDecisions.context: The codebase is split. The one books-feature component consumed by other features takes a labels object (BookMultiSelectPickerLabels, book-multi-select-picker.tsx:24-34; caller supplies them at loan-books-step.tsx:47-56 and create-book-order-dialog.tsx:144). The two in-feature single-select pickers call useTranslations on their own namespace (dedication-book-picker-dialog.tsx:67 -> dedications.picker, add-book-to-queue-dialog -> its own block). Quotes already owns `quotes.bookPicker` {clear, empty, heading, loadMore, searching} in uk.json and en.json.
options: (a) labels prop; Quotes keys live under quotes.dialog.bookPicker (rename/reuse the existing quotes.bookPicker block).
(b) The picker calls useTranslations on a new shared namespace, e.g. books.singleSelectPicker, and callers pass nothing.
openDecisions.recommendation: (a) - it is the only precedent for a books-feature component crossing feature boundaries, and it keeps each caller's copy in its own namespace.
openDecisions.answer: (a) labels prop, following book-multi-select-picker.tsx:24-34. Quotes keys live under quotes.dialog.bookPicker (rename/reuse the existing quotes.bookPicker block). Decided by the orchestrator.

openDecisions.question: Do we migrate the two existing single-select pickers onto the new component in this PR?
openDecisions.context: This is the third implementation of the same control: DedicationBookPickerDialog (dedication-book-picker-dialog.tsx:37) and AddBookToQueueDialog (add-book-to-queue-dialog.tsx:44) both do RadioGroup + useLibraryBooks + sort title_asc + pageSize 20 + a local PickerCover copy. docs/code-principles.md §0.0 lever 5 says standardize on the third real use. The spec never asks for it; it only forbids importing or copying the Dedications component.
options: (a) Ship the Quotes refactor only; log a follow-up to migrate the other two.
(b) Migrate all three in this PR - removes two duplicates, but adds the dedications and reading-queue flows (and their tests) to the review surface.
openDecisions.recommendation: (a). Keep the diff auditable against this spec; the duplicates are already noted and can be removed in a follow-up PR with their own tests.
openDecisions.answer: (a) Ship Quotes only. Do not migrate dedication-book-picker-dialog.tsx or add-book-to-queue-dialog.tsx in this PR; log a follow-up. Decided by the orchestrator.

openDecisions.question: What type crosses the picker boundary for the selected book?
openDecisions.context: The list yields `BookView`, but Quotes' edit mode only has `QuoteView.book` = `{ cover, firstAuthorName, id, title }` (packages/shared/src/quotes.ts:136-141), which cannot be widened into a BookView. Quotes already has a mapper `toQuoteBookOption` (apps/web/src/features/quotes/model/quote-book.ts:10).
options: (a) `value: Nullable<BookSelectOption>` (minimal {id,title,authorName,cover}) for display + `onChange(book: BookView)` so callers keep full data; Quotes maps with toQuoteBookOption.
(b) `value: Nullable<string>` (id only) and the caller renders the compact state - incompatible with D4 option (a).
(c) `value` and `onChange` both use the minimal option type - simplest, but throws away the BookView a caller might need.
openDecisions.recommendation: (a). It satisfies both call sites, keeps the compact card inside the picker, and reuses the existing mapper.
openDecisions.answer: (a) value: Nullable<BookSelectOption>, onChange receives the picked BookView, the caller maps through the existing toQuoteBookOption (features/quotes/model/quote-book.ts:10). Decided by the orchestrator.

2026-09-17: review round. code-reviewer returned NEEDS CHANGES with two criticals: (1) maxPages lived in query options, not the key, and the picker shared a byte-identical key with AddBookToQueueDialog, so last-observer-wins poisoned the shared entry; reworked into LIBRARY_BOOKS_RETENTION with retention as part of the key. (2) Radix RadioGroup clicks on focus while an arrow key is held, so every arrow keypress selected a book and collapsed the picker; reworked into explicit view state plus a pointer/keyboard discriminator in the capture phase plus deliberate focus transfer.

2026-09-17: perf audit (production build, Playwright + CDP). Critical: reopening the dialog after staleTime refetched every retained page sequentially, 50 requests / 10s at depth; fixed with staleTime Infinity on the whole-library retention (measured 11 requests -> 0). Warning: every keystroke re-rendered all retained rows, 0.083*N ms; fixed with a memoized BookSingleSelectRow (1000 rows: 68.7ms -> 1.3ms). Virtualization rejected: scroll was already smooth at 16.7ms median because max-h-64 paints only 256px.

2026-09-17: accessibility audit. Keyboard fix verified empirically (40 arrows, list stays open, bodyHits 0, keyboard-only paging 20->40->60). Eight findings fixed in-scope: opacity-60 contrast failure (21 light / 11 dark axe violations -> 0), role=status trapped inside aria-busy plus unannounced append, focus lost to body after a failed submit, aria-required false on the radiogroup, focus ring on the 16x16 dot instead of the row, duplicated field name on the search input, dangling htmlFor when collapsed, and the collapsed view not conveying its value.

2026-09-17: OUT OF SCOPE, needs a separate task.
